body:
APPLICABLE BEHAVIOUR: the observation cursor is a single GLOBAL, filter-independent durable position in the ledger's commit order — not per-subscription.

Which integration this is
- This workspace is Palimpsest; its "integration" is the Ordarium consumer boundary pinned in package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides to release `ordarium-v1.3.1` (installed: @ordarium/core 1.3.1, @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1, @ordarium/host-kit 1.3.1). Docs in-repo are stale at the 1.2.0 baseline (07 r19), so the pinned artifact, not the docs, is the governing source for the dependency interface.

The apparent conflict
- docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md asserts cursor positions are "per-subscription, not global", but self-describes as: "informational, not normative" and "not updated against the current pinned artifact".
- The pinned artifact says the opposite (below).

Local resolution under the repo's own precedence rule
- docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md (PLMP-ALN-2) rule 1: the published contract of the exact pinned version (shipped type declarations / release specification) governs that interface's behaviour; rule 3: informational records (engineering notes, historical alignment records) are explanatory only and never override 1 or 2.
- So rule 1 beats rule 3. No genuinely unresolved load-bearing conflict remains, and the note itself concedes it is stale, so no cross-repo escalation was warranted.

What the pinned contract actually specifies
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 dist/src/types.d.ts, StateChangePage.cursor: "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" (always present, unlike the nextCursor? pagination of other read surfaces).
- StateChangeFilter (namespace/limit) only narrows which changes are delivered; limit caps the page. It does not define a per-subscription coordinate.
- ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 changes(): "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; cursor encodes {c: change_seq}; positions advance over the global commit order (filtering skips non-matching entries but the cursor still advances past them); a restored/replaced ledger lowers the high-water mark and the cursor fails closed with InvalidCursorError (INVALID_CURSOR), distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT.
- The volatile MemoryLedger in @ordarium/core uses the same semantics: contiguous global positions 1..n, namespace filter applied after position iteration, cursor = last delivered global position, and after > high-water throws InvalidCursorError.

Conclusion
- For this integration the applicable observation-cursor behaviour is the pinned 1.3.1 contract: one opaque, ledger-wide, filter-independent durable resume position (plus fail-closed INVALID_CURSOR on a foreign/restored/replaced ledger). The per-subscription reading in cursor-note.md does not apply: it is a non-normative, explicitly stale informational record superseded for interface behaviour by source-precedence rule 1.
- Note the workspace does not yet consume the change feed (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts uses store.list pagination nextCursor, not store.changes), so this is a contract-interpretation determination, not a current code path; any future consumer must treat the cursor as global/filter-independent.
